workflowGraph.self_edge: A node cannot link to itself unless the link is a loop.
workflowGraph.cycle: The graph contains a cycle. Ordinary links cannot go backwards — use a loop link for that.
workflowGraph.dangling_edge: A link refers to a node that does not exist.
workflowGraph.duplicate_edge: These two nodes are already linked.
workflowGraph.reserved_node_key: This node key is reserved for the supervisor phase.
workflowGraph.invalid_loop_edge: A loop link must lead to a preceding node or to the node itself.
workflowGraph.overlapping_loop_bodies: Loop bodies must not overlap or share nodes.
workflowGraph.loop_body_requires_confirmation: A node marked “Requires confirmation” cannot be inside a loop.
workflowGraph.loop_body_fan_out: Only the last node of a loop (where the loop link starts) may lead outside it.

support.title: Customer support reply
support.description: Prepare a policy-compliant response to a delayed delivery, ready for an operator to send.
support.prompt: Draft an English reply to Maya about order A-1042. Delivery was promised on October 20; today is October 24. Carrier update: delayed at sorting center, estimated delivery October 26. Our supplied policy allows a shipping-fee refund after more than two days of delay. The fee was EUR 8. Product refunds require a carrier investigation. Apologize, explain the available option and ask for consent. Do not claim a refund was already issued.
support.output: A customer reply citing order A-1042, the carrier’s October 26 estimate and the EUR 8 shipping-fee refund option, plus an operator note about uncertainties. No email is sent and no refund is issued.
support.connections: Check facts → Draft reply → Review reply. Each step waits for its predecessor. Optional confirmation on the review step pauses before review starts.

0.name: Check facts and policy
0.instruction: Extract the order ID, promised and estimated delivery dates, delay duration, supplied policy and allowed remedy. List prohibited claims. Use only the user request.

1.name: Draft the customer reply
1.instruction: Use the predecessor facts to write a concise, empathetic reply. Present the carrier date as an estimate, offer the supplied remedy and ask for consent. Do not invent refunds or investigation outcomes.

2.name: Review the reply
2.instruction: Check the draft against the supplied facts and policy. Return a corrected customer reply and a short operator note on uncertainty. Do not send anything or issue a refund.

campaign.title: Workshop campaign plan
campaign.description: Combine two parallel specialists into a practical campaign with content, a budget and metrics.
campaign.prompt: Prepare a campaign for a free 45-minute online workshop, “Automate your weekly reports”, on November 12 at 14:00 UTC. Audience: operations leads in teams of 10–50. Available channels: 800 opted-in email contacts and the company LinkedIn page. Target: 40 registrations. Budget: EUR 300. Deliver a seven-day schedule, three LinkedIn post drafts, one email draft and success metrics. Do not access accounts or promise registrations.
campaign.output: A seven-day campaign schedule, three post drafts, one email draft, budget allocation of at most EUR 300 and measurable registration metrics. Nothing is published or sent.
campaign.connections: Audience analysis and Content angles run independently, up to two at once. Both connect to Campaign plan, which waits for both successful results.

0.name: Analyze the audience
0.instruction: Analyze the supplied audience, reporting pain points, constraints and registration target. Separate assumptions from supplied facts. Do not invent market statistics.

1.name: Develop content angles
1.instruction: Propose three content angles for the supplied workshop, each with a value proposition, likely objection and call to action. Preserve the event details. Do not publish.

2.name: Build the campaign plan
2.instruction: Combine both predecessor results into a seven-day schedule with three LinkedIn drafts, one email draft, budget totaling at most EUR 300 and measurable registration metrics. Clearly label proposals.

incident.title: Technical incident assessment
incident.description: Turn supplied logs into an evidence-based diagnosis and a reversible recovery plan.
incident.prompt: Deployment app-v42 completed at 09:12 UTC, followed by proxy 502 errors. Proxy log: connect() failed (111: Connection refused) to upstream http://app:8000/health. New application log: Server listening on 0.0.0.0:8080. The previous deployment listened on port 8000. No database errors appear in the supplied excerpt. Assess the incident and propose a reversible recovery plan. You have no cluster access. Do not execute commands or claim recovery.
incident.output: A diagnosis grounded in the observed 8000/8080 port mismatch, a verification checklist and a reversible recovery proposal. No infrastructure checks or changes are executed.
incident.connections: Extract evidence → Rank hypotheses → Draft runbook. The supervisor combines the completed work into the final assessment.

0.name: Extract incident evidence
0.instruction: Build a timeline and list observed facts, unknowns and the relevant port mismatch. Treat the absence of a database error in this excerpt as limited evidence, not proof.

1.name: Rank likely causes
1.instruction: Use the predecessor evidence to rank plausible causes. Explain supporting facts and read-only checks that would distinguish the causes. Separate confidence from fact.

2.name: Draft a recovery runbook
2.instruction: Use the ranked causes to propose reversible recovery: verify listener/upstream configuration, align routing or roll back to the known previous deployment, verify health and traffic. Include prerequisites and rollback conditions. Claim no executed checks or recovery.
